episodes.187534: An atmospheric river event brought flooding, record breaking rainfall, and record high temperatures to Western Washington.
episodes.187572: A slow moving frontal system brought several days of heavy rain, which caused flooding on the Coquille River at Coquille.
episodes.187822: A pair of moderate atmospheric rivers brought heavy rain leading to minor river and urban flooding to portions of northwest Oregon.
episodes.187856: A strong atmospheric river brought heavy rains on December 5th which led to minor river and urban flooding across portions of southwest Washington. Clark County and Cowlitz County saw landslides, along with minor river flooding, including the Cowlitz River at Kelso and the Grays River near Rosburg. Portions of the Willapa Hills and south Washington Cascades received 12 to 16 inches of rain over a 5 day period beginning December 1st.

events.narrative: A record rainfall of 1.51 inches fell at the National Weather Service office in Seattle. This broke the previous daily record of 1.39 inches set in 1946.
A record rainfall of 4.19 inches was recorded at the Quillayute airport. This broke the previous daily record of 1.82 inches set in 1971.
A record rainfall of 2.93 inches at the Hoquiam Airport broke the previous daily record of 2.30 inches set in 1990.
A male age 53, drowned in Bronson Creek, SE of Hillsboro.

The Coquille River at Coquille rose above minor flood stage of 21.0 ft at 04/0830 PST, and crested at minor flood stage at 21.24 ft at 04/1900 PST. The river dropped below minor flood stage at 05/0030 PST.
The Grays River rose above flood stage on December 4th, cresting at 16.24 feet on December 5th at 9 am, and fell below flood stage on December 6th. Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
